conventions.convention: Pencils have positive order. Regularity means det(A−λB) is not the zero polynomial. Homogeneous eigenvalues are nonzero complex pairs [α:β] satisfying det(βA−αB)=0, modulo nonzero complex scaling; β=0 denotes infinity and σ(A,B) contains only finite ratios.
The B-inner product is linear first: ⟨x,y⟩B=y*Bx. For B=LL*, the primal norm is ||L*x||₂ and the dual residual norm is ||L⁻¹r||₂.

Complex generalized Schur form uses Q*AZ=S and Q*BZ=T with both factors triangular. Real form permits only one-by-one real blocks and two-by-two nonreal conjugate-root blocks in S, while T remains upper triangular.
Matrix indices start at zero. Left rotations annihilate the second coordinate of a column; first-coordinate row annihilation uses the reversal/adjoint factor J L(conjugate(b),conjugate(a))* J.

A computed rotation is generated once and shared by both matrices. Its normalized exact unitary representative is recorded as a factor product. Structural target writes enter the arithmetic allowance once; tolerance deflations are separate exact perturbations without an O(u) assertion.

The QZ budget counts sweeps after initialization and deflation; N=0 permits no sweep. qz-computed requires triangular factors and nonzero diagonal pairs. Infinite candidates describe the returned perturbed pencil, and no unconditional convergence is asserted.

Residual certificates propagate raw stored-factor action errors, apply matvec bounds only to stored inputs, and evaluate allowances through an exact controller. Failure of the independent residual route does not invalidate a separately valid local-accumulation certificate.

load_bearing.statement: Successful common computed Givens actions admit exact unitary representatives and local pair bounds ℓP(C,D), with ℓ=η for matrix-target actions and ℓ=v for raw actions; the lemma also supplies a stored-factor-action residual certificate with explicit propagated allowances.

For the stated finite sequence of exact unitary two-sided updates with arithmetic and deflation perturbations, A_m=Q*(A+Δ_A)Z and B_m=Q*(B+Δ_B)Z, with combined Frobenius perturbation bounded by the sum of the local arithmetic pair norms and deflation pair norms; empty products are identities.

For Hermitian A and positive-definite Hermitian B=LL*, C=L⁻¹AL⁻* is self-adjoint with an orthonormal eigenbasis and real eigenvalues. The vectors x_i=L⁻*y_i satisfy Ax_i=λ_iBx_i and x_i*Bx_j=δ_ij; the homogeneous eigenvalues are exactly [λ_i:1], with none infinite.

For every input of alg-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-reduction, the algorithm terminates and returns orthogonal/unitary Q,Z, an upper Hessenberg matrix H, and an upper triangular matrix T such that H=Q*AZ and T=Q*BZ.
Every regular finite square pencil (A,B) over R or C has at least one homogeneous generalized eigenvalue pair [α:β] over C.
If (A,B) is a regular pencil and x∈Cⁿ satisfies Ax=0 and Bx=0, then x=0.
For a common block upper triangular pair with two positive block sizes, det(βA−αB)=det(βA₁₁−αB₁₁)det(βA₂₂−αB₂₂) for every complex α,β.

Every run of the specified finite-budget QZ algorithm terminates with a declared status. Successful initialization and completed sweeps preserve Hessenberg-triangular structure, except at explicitly isolated blocks. Certified exact-unitary factor records and local residuals give a two-sided equivalence to an accumulated perturbed input pair, without a size bound.

Checked B-metric uses in block LOBPCG and the Ritz lemmas, plus harmonic-extraction and termination uses of QZ.
